QuestionStmt.S: Calculate the work done in following reaction at 27°C. $$\mathrm{4SO_2(g) + 2O_2(g) \rightarrow 4SO_3(g)}$$ ($R = 8.314$ J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)

Solution.S:
Given reaction:

$$4SO_2(g) + 2O_2(g) \rightarrow 4SO_3(g)$$

## Step 1: Calculate $\Delta n_g$ (change in moles of gas):

Reactant gas moles: $4(SO_2) + 2(O_2) = 6$

Product gas moles: $4(SO_3)$

Therefore,

$$\Delta n_g = \text{Product gas moles} - \text{Reactant gas moles} = 4 - 6 = -2$$

## Step 2: Write the formula for work done ($W$) at constant temperature and pressure:

At constant pressure,

$$W = -P \Delta V$$

For gaseous reactions at constant $T$ and $P$,

$$\Delta V = \Delta n_g \cdot RT / P$$

So,

$$W = -\Delta n_g \cdot RT$$

## Step 3: Substitute the values:

$$\Delta n_g = -2$$

$$R = 8.314 \, \text{J K}^{-1} \, \text{mol}^{-1}$$

$$T = 27^\circ \text{C} = 27 + 273 = 300 \, \text{K}$$

$$W = -(2) \times 8.314 \times 300$$

$$W = 2 \times 8.314 \times 300$$

$$W = 2 \times 2494.2 = 4988.4 \, \text{J}$$

## Final Answer:

$$4988.4 \, \text{J}$$
